   Fire-ravaged regions in Indonesia face rising flood threat
 Sign up now: Get insights on Asia's fast-moving developments
 The warning comes after months of drought and widespread forest and peatland fires, fuelled by prolonged dry conditions under the influence of El Nino.
 PHOTO: REUTERS
 Published   Nov 04, 2026, 11:28 AM
 Updated   Nov 04, 2026, 07:17 PM
 Set as preferred source Unlock audio Summarise Indonesia’s fire-hit regions now face a higher flood risk as the rainy season starts, because burned land and damaged peatlands cannot absorb water well.
 BNPB warned of flash floods and landslides, while BMKG said rain will begin in most areas between November and December, with El Nino possibly delaying the peak.
 Experts and activists urged peatland restoration and corporate accountability, but doubts remain over whether the revived peatland agency has enough power and resources.
 AI generated
 JAKARTA – After months of battling forest and peatland fires, parts of Indonesia face another threat as damaged landscapes leave communities increasingly vulnerable to flooding ahead of the rainy season.
 The National Disaster Mitigation Agency (BNPB) on Nov 3 urged residents nationwide to prepare for hydrometeorological disasters, including flash floods and landslides, as parts of the country enter the rainy season.
